    • parents

      public Map<String,Map<String,Set<String>>> parents
      All the cached "parent" relations of all transitive relations meaning the relations between all first arguments and the transitive closure of second arguments. The external HashMap pairs relation name String keys to values that are the parent relationships. The interior HashMap is the set of terms and their transitive closure of parents.

    • instanceOf

      public Map<String,Set<String>> instanceOf
      Parent relations from instances, including those that are transitive through (instance,instance) relations, such as subAttribute and subrelation. May not do what you think since the key is the child (instance)

    • children

      public Map<String,Map<String,Set<String>>> children
      All the cached "child" relations of all transitive relations meaning the relations between all first arguments and the transitive closure of second arguments. The external HashMap pairs relation name String keys to values that are the child relationships. The interior HashMap is the set of terms and their transitive closure of children.

    • signatures

      public Map<String,List<String>> signatures
      Relation name keys and argument types with 0th arg always "" except in the case of Functions where the 0th arg will be the function range. Variable arity relations may have a type for the last argument, which will be the type repeated for all extended arguments. Note that types can be functions, rather than just terms. Note that types (when there's a domainSubclass etc) are designated by a '+' appended to the class name.

    • addSubclass

      public Set<String> addSubclass(String child, String parent)
      Incrementally record (subclass child parent). Updates: parents["subclass"] — child and all its descendants gain parent's ancestors children["subclass"] — parent and all its ancestors gain child's descendants instanceOf — instances of child/descendants gain parent's ancestors instances — parent and ancestors gain instances of child/descendants
      Parameters:
      child - the new subclass (e.g. "Robot")
      parent - the existing superclass (e.g. "Agent")
      Returns:
      the set of terms whose cache entries changed

    • addInstance

      public Set<String> addInstance(String inst, String className)
      Incrementally record (instance inst className). Updates: insts — inst is added as a known instance term instanceOf — inst gains className and all its subclass ancestors instances — className and all ancestors gain inst
      Parameters:
      inst - the new instance (e.g. "myRobot")
      className - the class (e.g. "Robot")
      Returns:
      the set of terms whose cache entries changed

    • addDomain

      public Set<String> addDomain(String relation, int argNum, String type)
      Incrementally record (domain relation argNum type) or (domainSubclass relation argNum type+). Updates: signatures — relation's argNum slot is set to type valences — updated if argNum exceeds current recorded arity signatures — all child relations (via subrelation) that lack an explicit argNum binding inherit type
      Parameters:
      relation - the relation (e.g. "loves")
      argNum - the argument position (1-based; 0 = range)
      type - the type string (append "+" for domainSubclass)
      Returns:
      the set of terms whose cache entries changed

    • addRange

      public Set<String> addRange(String relation, String type)
      Incrementally record (range relation type). Range is stored at position 0 of the signatures list.
      Parameters:
      relation - the relation (e.g. "motherOf")
      type - the range type (e.g. "Woman")
      Returns:
      the set of terms whose cache entries changed

    • addSubrelation

      public Set<String> addSubrelation(String child, String parent)
      Incrementally record (subrelation child parent). Updates: parents["subrelation"] — child and its sub-relations gain parent's ancestors children["subrelation"] — parent and its ancestors gain child's sub-relations signatures / valences — child inherits parent's domain declarations where the child has no explicit binding
      Parameters:
      child - the new sub-relation (e.g. "biologicalMother")
      parent - the existing parent relation (e.g. "mother")
      Returns:
      the set of terms whose cache entries changed

    • addDisjoint

      public Set<String> addDisjoint(String class1, String class2)
      Incrementally record (disjoint class1 class2). Updates: explicitDisjoint — symmetric entry added for class1↔class2 disjoint — all pairs of (subclasses of class1) × (subclasses of class2) are recorded as disjoint, in both orderings
      Parameters:
      class1 - first disjoint class
      class2 - second disjoint class
      Returns:
      the set of terms whose cache entries changed

    • p_buildCaches

      private void p_buildCaches()
      Parallel build using CompletableFuture with a dependency-wave graph. Wave 1 (independent, parallel): buildInsts, buildRelationsSet, buildTransitiveRelationsSet, buildDirectParentTerms Wave 2 (after Wave 1, parallel with each other): buildParents (needs transRels), buildChildren (needs transRels) Wave 3 (after Wave 2, parallel with each other): collectDomains (needs relations+parents), buildDirectInstances (needs parents) Wave 4 (sequential, after Wave 3): buildInstTransRels → addTransitiveInstances → buildTransInstOf + correctValences → buildFunctionsSet → [disjoint group] → storeCacheAsFormulas → buildSymbolTaxonomy

    • _buildCaches

      Conventional/sequential version (kept for reference and fallback)

    • copyNewPredFromVariableArity

      public void copyNewPredFromVariableArity(String pred, String oldPred, int arity)
      Copy all relevant information from a VariableArityRelation to a new predicate that is a particular fixed arity. Fill the signature from final argument type in the predicate. Uses double-checked locking: the first containsKey() is a thread-safe read on ConcurrentHashMap (fast path, no lock). Only the first registration for each (pred,arity) pair acquires the monitor; all subsequent calls return immediately.
